definitions.gloss: to start over; to reset; to make a fresh start
definitions.explanation: To go back to the beginning and try again from scratch, especially after a failed attempt or stalled situation. Originally a sumo term for resetting a bout when wrestlers fail to charge properly.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}を{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}そう。
{交渉|こうしょう}がうまくいかなかったので、{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}すことにした。
examples.english: The negotiations didn't go well, so we decided to start fresh.

examples.japanese: {一度|いちど}{気持|きも}ちをリセットして、ゼロから{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}したほうがいいと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think it's better to reset your mindset and start over from zero.

notes:
Originally from sumo wrestling, where {仕切|しき}り{直|なお}し refers to the wrestlers returning to their starting positions to retry the initial charge ({立|た}ち{合|あ}い) when they fail to synchronize. The word has been widely adopted in everyday and business Japanese to mean starting over.

USAGE:
Often used when a project, negotiation, or plan has stalled or failed and needs to be restarted from the beginning. Carries a positive, proactive nuance — the speaker is choosing to try again rather than giving up.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {計画|けいかく}を{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}す — to restart a plan
- {交渉|こうしょう}を{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}す — to restart negotiations
- {仕切|しき}り{直|なお}しになる — to become a do-over
- ゼロから{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}す — to start over from zero

SIMILAR WORDS:
- やり{直|なお}す — to redo; more general, applies to any task or action
- {出直|でなお}す — to start fresh; implies going away and coming back to try again
- {白紙|はくし}に{戻|もど}す — to return to a blank slate; emphasizes canceling everything decided so far
